{{Short description|Suffragette supporters boycotting the census}}
{{More citations needed|section|date=April 2025}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2025}}{{use British English|date=April 2025}}
[[File:Suffragettes boycotting 1911 census in Manchester.jpg|thumb|Suffragettes boycotting 1911 census in [[Manchester]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rogers |first=Simon |date=2012-12-11 |title=Census in pictures: from suffragettes to arms protesters |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/datablog/gallery/2012/dec/11/census-2011-pictures-suffragettes-arms-protesters |access-date=2026-07-21 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>]]
These [[Women's suffrage in the United Kingdom|British suffragettes and suffragists]] are known to have participated in a [[1911 United Kingdom census#Suffragette boycott|boycott of the 1911 United Kingdom census]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dobraszczyk |first=Paul |date=2009-01-01 |title=‘Give in your account’: Using and Abusing Victorian Census Forms |url=https://doi.org/10.3366/E1355550209000575 |journal=Journal of Victorian Culture |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=1–25 |doi=10.3366/E1355550209000575 |issn=1355-5502|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Liddington |first=Jill |last2=Crawford |first2=Elizabeth |author-link2=Elizabeth Crawford (historian) |date=2011-03-01 |title=‘Women do not count, neither shall they be counted’: Suffrage, Citizenship and the Battle for the 1911 Census |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/hwj/dbq064 |journal=History Workshop Journal |volume=71 |issue=1 |pages=98–127 |doi=10.1093/hwj/dbq064 |issn=1363-3554|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Liddington">{{Cite book |last=Liddington |first=Jill |title=Vanishing for the vote: suffrage, citizenship and the battle for the census |last2=Crawford |first2=Elizabeth |date=2014 |isbn=9780719087486 |language=English |oclc=861673182}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Frangoul |first=Phoebe |date=2021-03-20 |title=The Secret Feminist History Of The Census (And Why Statues Of Women Matter) |url=https://graziadaily.co.uk/life/real-life/census-sufragettes-emily-wilding-davison/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Grazia |language=en}}</ref> The number of boycotters has been estimated to have been in the thousands, but was probably fewer than 100,000 in total.<ref name="Liddington" />

Notable women who participated in the boycott include:

* [[Laura Ainsworth]], 38 other women and one man [[Laura Ainsworth#If women don't count, then they were not going to be counted|sought to hide]] in [[Jezreel's Tower]] in [[Gillingham, Kent]], but they were betrayed and still counted by census officials.<ref name="wahs">{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Elizabeth |title=Laura Ainsworth |url=https://womanandhersphere.com/tag/laura-ainsworth/ |access-date=2017-12-04 |website=Woman and her Sphere |language=en}}</ref><ref name="bbc">{{Cite news |date=2011-03-20 |title=Medway women boycott 1911 census |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/local/kent/hi/people_and_places/newsid_9424000/9424365.stm |access-date=2017-12-03 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* [[Rhoda Anstey]]: participated on behalf of the [[Anstey College of Physical Education]], which she had founded in 1897<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Elizabeth |date=2013-04-02 |title=Suffrage Stories: An Entire Birmingham College Boycotts The 1911 Census |url=https://womanandhersphere.com/2013/04/02/suffrage-stories-an-entire-birmingham-college-boycotts-the-1911-census/ |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=Woman and her Sphere |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Elkes |first=Neil |date=2018-02-06 |title=Suffragette city: How three inspiring Birmingham women helped win the vote 100 years ago |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/fires-force-feeding-fury-birminghams-14238113 |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=Birmingham Live |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gauld |first=Nicola |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=beBqDwAAQBAJ&dq=rhoda+anstey&pg=PT81 |title=Words and Deeds: Birmingham Suffragists and Suffragettes 1832-1918 |date=2018-08-19 |publisher=History West Midlands |isbn=978-1-905036-48-6 |language=en}}{{page needed|date=November 2024}}</ref> 
* [[Helen Archdale]]: hosted a mass census boycott party with Adela Pankhurst<ref name=":1" />
* [[Hertha Ayrton]]: hosted a boycott party for approximately 40 people at her home in 41 Norfolk Square.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sharp |first=Evelyn |url=http://archive.org/details/hertha-ayrton-1854-1923-a-memoir |title=Hertha Ayrton, 1854-1923: A Memoir |date=1926}}</ref> Wrote on census form: "How can I answer all these questions if I have not the intelligence to choose between two candidates or parliament? I will not supply these particulars until I have my rights as a citizen. Votes for Women."<ref name="Liddington" />
* [[Minnie Baldock]]: did not appear on the census, although her husband and sons were enumerated<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-09 |title=Suffragettes in Canning Town |url=https://www.newhamheritagemonth.org/records/suffragettes-in-canning-town/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Newham Heritage Month |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* [[Inez Bensusan]]: member of the [[Actresses' Franchise League]] who performed during a mass evasion party<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inez Bensusan |url=http://orlando.cambridge.org/public/svPeople?person_id=bensin |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201031339/http://orlando.cambridge.org/public/svPeople?person_id=bensin |archive-date=2017-12-01 |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=© Orlando Project |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Rosa May Billinghurst]]
* [[Mary Blathwayt]]
* Dorothy Bowker: wrote: "Dumb Politically, Blind to the Census, Deaf to the Enumerator. Being classed with criminals lunatics & paupers I prefer to give no further particulars''"''<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=1911 UK Census Collection |url=https://www.thegenealogist.co.uk/census/1911/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=The Genealogist}}</ref>
* [[Nina Boyle]]: wrote "No Votes. No Census. Votes for Women" on her census form<ref>{{Cite web |last=Etayo |first=Oihane |title=Constance Antonia 'Nina' Boyle |url=https://map.mappingwomenssuffrage.org.uk/items/show/246 |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Mapping Women's Suffrage, [[University of Warwick]]}}</ref>
* [[Georgina Brackenbury]]: hosted an evasion party for 25 women and 1 man. 
* [[Marie Brackenbury]]: hosted an evasion party for 25 women and 1 man. Wrote on the census form: "Miss Marie Brackenbury in charge takes this opportunity of registering her protest against the votelessness of the women of Great Britain by refusing to fill in this form."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Georgina & Marie Brackenbury |url=https://map.mappingwomenssuffrage.org.uk/items/show/336 |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Mapping Women's Suffrage, University of Warwick}}</ref>

* [[Emily Davison]]: hid in the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] and was thus registered as an "occupant" of the [[Palace of Westminster]] and enumerated in Parliament<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=No Vote, No Census - 1911 Census Protests |url=https://www.historic-uk.com/HistoryUK/HistoryofBritain/No-Vote-No-Census-1911-Census-Protests/ |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Historic UK |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=The Palace of Westminster Official Guide|year=2012|publisher=Houses of Parliament|page=17|isbn=978-0-95620-292-5}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Emily Wilding Davison and Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.uk/about/living-heritage/transformingsociety/electionsvoting/womenvote/case-studies-women-parliament/ewd/ |access-date=17 November 2024 |website=UK Parliament}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=How we uncovered suffragette Emily Davison hiding in Parliament's crypt in the 1911 Census {{!}} Blog |url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/blog/discoveries/astonishing-1911-census-find-emily-davison-in-parliaments-crypt |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Find My Past |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Smith |first=Simon |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/The_British_Census/kugbEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=boycotted+the+1911+census&pg=PA45&printsec=frontcover |title=The British Census |date=2021-05-27 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing |isbn=978-1-78442-455-8 |language=en}}</ref>

* [[Bessie Drysdale]]: wrote on her form: "as the Government refuses me a vote and as I am not therefore recognised as a citizen, I refuse to perform the duties of one in giving the information required by the Government"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stenlake |first=Frances |title=Bessie Drysdale |url=https://map.mappingwomenssuffrage.org.uk/items/show/347 |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Mapping Women's Suffrage, University of Warwick}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Collection : Suffragists & Suffragettes [SUFCOL1] |url=https://hgsheritage.org.uk/Detail/collections/SUFCOL1 |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Hampstead Garden Suburb Virtual Museum}}</ref>
